1.

Safer can no one be Than God’s little child-gathering; Over it He has compassion, Bears it in His Father’s arms.

2.

No distress and no fortune Shall from His hand us snatch, He, our Friend beyond other friends, His children’s cares knows.

3.

Rejoice then, thou little gathering! God His own shall preserve; Before His will must all Enemies to the earth fall.

4.

What He takes and what He gives, The same Father He remains, And His aim is but the one— The child’s true welfare alone.

5.

Praise be to Thee, our God and Father, That our song of praise Thou dost receive! Grace’s riches we have tasted, Which Thou never dost withdraw.

6.

And at last, when hence we journey Through heaven’s bright clouds, Shall we Thee better praise For Thy great gift of grace.
